items.title: Email Campaign · : Referral Push (30-60 Day Post-Install)
items.preview:
**Highest conversion bet of the week.** These 30 people just spent real money, the install glow is fresh, and the ask is a favor + cash, not a sell.
**1. Campaign name + audience:** "Fresh Install Referral Push". 30 recipients (30-60 days post-install, satisfied)
**2. Subject line + alternates (60 char max):**
- Primary: `Who do you know with bad water?` (pain)
- Alt 1: `There's $500 in this email` (specific)
- Alt 2: `A quick favor (worth $500 to you)` (curiosity)
- Alt 3: `The best compliment you can give us` (curiosity)
- Alt 4: `How our best clients get paid` (authority)
**3. Preview text (90 char max):** `Refer a neighbor, we handle the rest. $500 when they join the ClearWave family.`
**4. Email body:**
Hi [First Name],
It's been about [X weeks] since we installed your ClearWave system, and we hope the water has been exactly what you hoped for.
Here's something most of our clients don't know: the people we install for almost always know someone else fighting the same water problems they used to have. A neighbor on the same well. A coworker across town. Family down the street.
So here's our thank-you for sending them our way.
When someone you refer books a free water assessment and becomes a client, you get **$500 cash**. Refer more than five in a year and it climbs to $750, then $1,000 at ten and up. And if someone you send just books the consult but isn't ready yet, that's still a **$50 gift card** for you.
No limit on how many friends you help. No catch.
Just reply to this email with a name and the best way to reach them, or forward this along and have them mention you. We take it from there.
Thank you for trusting us with your home.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave
*(Merge note: use install-date math for [X weeks]. All recipients named with current brand names or "your ClearWave system" per Rule 2. Anna Thompson = "your Meridian," Katie Helbling = "your Clearwave Crest," Wilhelmina Johnson/unspecified = "your ClearWave system." Amy Angelopoulos's legacy "Re-Ionator Pro Ultra" is NEVER printed. Tenure line only.)*
**5. Send timing:** Tuesday, 10:00 AM ET (post-Monday-inbox clear, pre-lunch peak).
**6. Expected performance:**
- Open: **48-55%.** Small, warm, recently-engaged segment vastly outperforms your all-list blasts. These people opened your install/completion comms weeks ago.
- Click/reply: **4-8%.** A dollar-value favor ask to satisfied new clients converts far above your 0.28% baseline (which is dragged down by cold mass sends).
- Conversion: **2-4 referred names**, realistically 1-2 closing over 60-90 days = $500-$1,000 pipeline from one send to 30 people.
**7. Source justification:** Draws on the **Referral Push candidate trigger** (30-60 day segment) and the **Referral Bonus Structure** (exact $500/$750/$1,000 + $50 gift card). Uses "free water assessment" per Rule 3a, pushes referrals not reviews per Rule 3.

items.title: Email Campaign · : Concierge "Is It Worth It?" (Year 1.5 Candidates)
items.preview:
**Biggest audience + biggest recurring-revenue upside.** 100 people, all past their year-1 service (trust established, floor cleared), likely DIY or pay-as-you-go. $99/mo recurring makes even a modest conversion materially valuable.
**1. Campaign name + audience:** "Is Concierge Worth It? (The Year 1.5 Math)". 100 recipients (13-24 months post-install, not on Concierge)
**2. Subject line + alternates (60 char max):**
- Primary: `The question we get at month 18` (curiosity)
- Alt 1: `Is Concierge actually worth it? Here's the math` (specific)
- Alt 2: `What your year-2 water costs (and how to fix it)` (pain)
- Alt 3: `Should you be on Concierge? Honest answer inside` (authority)
- Alt 4: `About that filter swap you've been meaning to do` (pain)
**3. Preview text (90 char max):** `No pressure. Just the honest math on whether Concierge saves you money and hassle.`
**4. Email body:**
Hi [First Name],
It's been about [X months] since we installed your ClearWave system, so you're right in the window where we get this question a lot:
"Is this Concierge thing actually worth it for me?"
Fair question. Here's the honest math, no pressure either way.
Concierge is $99/mo. For that you get your annual service handled, filter swaps done for you, priority phone support, and parts coverage on your standard install components. If you're the kind of person who'd rather never think about when the next filter is due, or chase down parts, it tends to pay for itself in convenience alone.
If you'd rather stay pay-as-you-go, that's completely fine too. Your system is built to run clean with minimal attention.
But if "I've been meaning to deal with that" sounds familiar, Concierge exists to make it disappear.
Want the breakdown for your specific setup? Just reply and I'll have someone walk you through it.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave
*(Merge note: tenure line via install-date math for all. Jessica & John Allen / Judith & Ralph Doll / Daniel Watson / Gunaseelan Muthukrishnan all hold legacy or component names. NEVER printed; use "your ClearWave system" + tenure line. All candidates confirmed 13-24 months, clearing the 12-month hard floor.)*
**5. Send timing:** Thursday, 11:00 AM ET (mid-week, decision-mode, separated from Proposal 1 so the two sends don't fatigue any overlap).
**6. Expected performance:**
- Open: **40-48%.** Established clients past their year-1 service, so the relationship is warm and the subject is curiosity-led, not salesy.
- Click/reply: **2-4%.** Soft "reply for the breakdown" ask + genuine opt-out language reduces resistance.
- Conversion: **2-5 Concierge sign-ups** at $99/mo = **$2,400-$6,000 annual recurring** from one send. Even the low end dwarfs a one-time campaign's value.
**7. Source justification:** Draws on the **Concierge Upsell candidate trigger** and the **Concierge Upsell Context** (exact $99/mo, "year 1.5 is-it-worth-it" framing, "here's the math" tone). Respects Hard Rule 1 (12-month floor) because the list is pre-filtered to 13-24 months. Uses tenure line per Rule 2.
---
## Why these two (and what I skipped)
- **Skipped the full-list / cold-lead blast this week.** Your 1,000 cold subscribers are worth re-engaging, but firing another broad send right now risks deepening the deliverability hole shown in recent 0.4% opens. I'd recommend a dedicated cold re-engagement campaign as a standalone next week, with a fresh water-news value hook and list-cleaning built in, so we don't contaminate these two warm sends.
- **Skipped the 1-year annual service group (12 people)** as its own campaign this week since it's small and operational; it folds naturally into a Jobber service reminder rather than a marketing push.
Want me to build the cold re-engagement draft for next week, or adjust segmentation on either of these?
